info.name: OAS Auth Service
info.description:
Auth-service (:8080), the user-catalogue (:8082) and Keycloak (:8180).

The catalogue owns users and password hashes. Keycloak stores no password at all - it calls the catalogue on every login. This service owns tokens and their revocation.

FOLDERS 0-5 are for stepping through by hand. Request bodies carry literal placeholders such as PASTE_USER_ID_HERE, which you replace with values copied from the previous response. Each request description says what to copy and what to expect.

FOLDER 6 is automated and self-chaining. Run it to verify the whole system in one click:
  newman run OAS_Auth_Service.postman_collection.json \
    -e OAS_Auth_Service.postman_environment.json \
    --folder "6. Regression (Automated)"

Note the catalogue stores password HASHES (the portal hashes before submission), so Create User sends a bcrypt hash while Token Create sends the plaintext.

Select the 'OAS Auth Service - Local' environment before running.

item.name: 0. Preflight
item.description:
Confirms all three services are reachable before anything else is attempted. Nothing downstream can work if one of these fails, so run this folder first.

These three carry assertions and need nothing pasted.

request.description: The auth-service itself. Owns no database, so this only depends on the app being up.
Confirms the OAS realm exists. If this 404s, run ./setup-realm.sh.
The user-catalogue. Keycloak calls it on every login, so login fails closed without it.

item.name: 1. User Lifecycle (catalogue side)
item.description:
What the user-catalogue owns. Three steps: create (PENDING) -> approve (APPROVED) -> review (ACTIVE). Only the last one touches Keycloak, and it pushes the user there BEFORE persisting ACTIVE, so a Keycloak outage cannot leave a live user who cannot log in.

Copy result.userId from the first response into every request that follows.

request.description:
Creates a PENDING user.

`password` is a bcrypt HASH, not plaintext: the catalogue's contract is that the portal hashes before submission. The hash above is for 'DemoPass#2026!'.

COPY result.userId.

Change the email if you run this twice; Keycloak requires unique addresses and the publish would fail on the second attempt.

Expect 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS.

The password is correct. The user is not published, so it does not exist in Keycloak at all - the maker-checker gate holds by construction rather than by a flag.
PENDING -> APPROVED. Still not in Keycloak; Login Before Approval still returns 401.

APPROVED -> ACTIVE, and the only step that touches Keycloak.

Keycloak is written first. Stop the Keycloak container and try this to see it return 502 with the record left at APPROVED.
Paste the userId into the URL. Status is at result.result.status and should read ACTIVE.

The endpoint Keycloak calls on every login. Expect valid:true plus userId, orgId, entityType.

Internal only - it accepts plaintext passwords and must not be exposed through Kong.

item.name: 2. Auth Service API
item.description:
The deliverable: four endpoints on :8080.

The fourth endpoint, auth_user_revoke, is exercised in folder 5 where its effect can be seen.

request.description:
Plaintext password here. Keycloak holds no credential for this user - it calls the catalogue's verify_credentials to check it.

COPY result.access_token and result.refresh_token.

Paste the access token into jwt.io: user_id, org_id and entity_type all came from the catalogue.

Expect 200 with active:true and the catalogue identifiers.

Entirely local: the signature is checked against Keycloak's published key, with no network call.

Denylists the token and its session, then ends the Keycloak session. refreshToken is optional.

Expect {"localRevocation": "ok", "idpLogout": "ok"}.

Same token as before. Expect 401 AUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED.

This is the point of the Redis denylist: Keycloak cannot recall a token it already issued, so without this the token would keep working until it expired.

item.name: 3. Credential Rejections
item.description:
All three return byte-identical bodies. Distinguishing them would allow username enumeration, and 'account is locked' tells an attacker their guessing is working.

Compare the three responses side by side.

request.description: Expect {"valid": false}.
A user id that does not exist. Identical body to Wrong Password.
Block a user in folder 5 first, then paste its id. Correct password, still identical.
The auth-service collapses them too. Expect 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS - identical for a wrong password, an unknown user, and a blocked account.

item.name: 4. Token Rejections
item.description: Every way a token can be refused by the auth-service.

request.description:
Expect 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID.

A refresh token is signed with the same key and passes the signature, issuer and azp checks. Only the typ == Bearer check stops it being accepted as proof of identity.
Take a real access token and change one character in the middle section. Expect 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID - the signature no longer matches.
Not a JWT at all. Expect 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID, not a 500.
Expect 400 AUTH_INVALID_REQUEST. A missing field is a bad request, not an auth failure.
Expect 400 AUTH_INVALID_REQUEST.

item.name: 5. Block Lifecycle
item.description:
Blocking an account takes three actions, and each covers a gap the others cannot:

  catalogue INACTIVE    stops new logins; tokens already issued keep working
  Keycloak disable      ends sessions and refresh tokens; cannot recall an issued token
  auth_user_revoke      kills tokens already in circulation

The catalogue's toggle endpoint performs all three. Run this folder last: it leaves the user blocked for 900 seconds.

request.description: Get a fresh token. COPY result.access_token - you will validate it after the block.
The auth-service endpoint the catalogue calls when blocking. Kills every live session for the user, including tokens issued after this call, for 900 seconds.
The token from Login. Expect 401 AUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED.

Paste the userId into the URL. Toggles ACTIVE <-> INACTIVE and performs all three actions.

Expect result.status INACTIVE. The Keycloak disable and the token revocation are best-effort and are not reported in the body - the catalogue status alone already blocks every new login, so a Keycloak blip must not fail the block. The two requests that follow are what show they happened.
Expect 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS. The catalogue is now INACTIVE, so verify_credentials refuses and no new token is issued at all.
Toggles back to ACTIVE. Sessions revoked above stay dead until their denylist entries expire - revocation is deliberately not undone.

item.name: 6. Regression (Automated)
item.description:
Self-chaining; nothing to paste. Creates its own user each run, so it is repeatable.

  newman run OAS_Auth_Service.postman_collection.json \
    -e OAS_Auth_Service.postman_environment.json \
    --folder "6. Regression (Automated)"

Requires the catalogue on :8082, Keycloak on :8180 and the auth-service on :8080.

exec: // Unique per run: Keycloak enforces unique email addresses.
